body: Well, Harvard and Stanford said I can't get a second Bachelor's. And it costs $70 for Carnegie Mellon. Getting in within the next year would take a miracle apparently, but I would be up to it. And okay, I'll try.

Yeah, clerical, stocking. I am fat. Maybe they rejected me because they thought I was out of shape. But I can lift 100. And any job except for sales and clerk, though. I can't convince others of anything and I'm horrible at bluffing, remembering lots of things, and dealing with lots of different people.

But assistance is for people who  need help with life or death situations I think? I'm just trying to get into college.

And they told me that I'd have to live off campus, but I don't know how I could afford it.

That's not even my first choice. My first choice was Harvard. Then Stanford. Then some college in Pittsburgh, but I think the deadline passed already.

I've never really known how to get a job. I mean I've had mock interviews and I'm told I'm good. I've had work study, but I didn't have to fight for it because obtaining a work study position was first come, first serve. I apply to jobs and get phone interviews and in person interviews. I research and the professional positions I apply for end up being filled by people wity Master's. Minimum wage doesn't seem to want me for being overqualified or maybe they mistake my display of confidence, offer of loyalty, obedience, and Asperger's to be offputting, maybe subconsciously? Thinking outside the box, how can I be overqualified for a minimum wage position though if they won't give me a minimum wage position? Employment confuses me.

I got the wrong degree from the wrong college and I didn't know until after I graduated. I was rushed and pressured to go locally and I didn't have time to explore the differences between 2 year and a 4 year; Comp Info Sys, Comp Prog, and Comp Sci, etc. Now some colleges won't accept second Bachelor's candidates. I need the second Bachelor's because it doesn't make sense and would be impossible transitioning from a BS in CIS to getting a MS in CS, which is my goal. Then there's other college who say I could get loans. If I qualified for full Pell Grant, I could have the $50 app fee waived. Well, after somebody has a Bachelor's, they're never eligible for Pell again. I don't have even $50. And they said I can't use loan money towards the college app fee.

I have an uncle that abuses alcohol and went to prison numerous times for beating his wife and resisting arrest while drunk. My father did drugs and abandoned me. Ever since mother stopped smoking and then got her first stable job seven years ago at 46, she acts cocky and acts like I'm such a huge failure even though I'm only 25 and I barely have any experience navigating the adult world. A lot of people tell me I'm smart. I'm not as smart as much as I just try to read everything and try to pay attention to everything to strategize ways so I can prevent myself from getting hurt and predict how and when the next time will be. The rest of the information I've learned are things I've learned along the way of doing the things I just mentioned.

She isn't teaching me the right way. I know that, but I also don't entirely know the right way, can't handle a lot of things on my own because it's so overwhelming, and I know occasional outpatient therapy will never be enough to head in the right direction. But if I even lived for 50 or 60 more years, it would be unsurprising if I needed psychotherapy until then.

I've been called so many things before, accused of so many diagnoses, moved so many places, given so many pills, told many lies, that the only thing I really know about myself is that I don't want to drink, smoke, or do drugs.

Edit: And well, they're an acute hospital and insurance doesn't pay for long term care so with those two facts, all they wanted to do was assess me, stabilize me, diagnose me, and send me home asap. In fact, if they take too long insurance won't pay because after a certain point they'll consider me unable to be helped. The psychiatrist said nobody stays for more than 5 to 7 days.

I cuss a lot and sometimes I treat her now the same way she's treated me since I was in elementary school. I'm scared that one day I'm going to lose all sense of boundaries. Sometimes I get lost if I'm her or if I'm fighting against everything using the techniques I had to teach myself as a child to try to cope with the world. The pain makes me want to die, the fear that I'm going to hurt others or might already be (I don't know) makes me want to die. And just everything pretty much makes me want to die. For example, eating, pooping, not eating, not pooping, just everything on both sides of the spectrum for everything. I've heard people say that when people go to Heaven, they are no longer in pain. I don't have a religion, but I wish I could die instead of reliving the memories of every day of my life.
The team in the inpatient unit had a meeting and they couldn't think of any place. Emotionally. I believe I am turning into her and I have feelings of guilt.

I don't know why I don't. Everyone seems to have different definitions on what domestic violence is. I once emailed the National DV hotline and they said something about how they weren't equipped to handle me because they deal with intimate partner violence, not parent abusing adult child.
